mainTopic: When do מצוות that say ביאה ('coming') and מושב ('dwelling') take effect, and what do these words teach in different מצוות
overview: The גמרא is studying רבי ישמעאל's rule about the words ביאה ('coming') and מושב ('dwelling'). First it narrows the rule: a מצוה waits until the land is conquered and settled only when both words appear together. It defends this reading against רבי עקיבא's challenge from שבת by explaining that רבי ישמעאל gave two answers. It then explains the practical difference between the two: whether נסכים were brought in the מדבר. Next אביי shows that another תנא of רבי ישמעאל's school learns from the מצוה of מלך that every 'coming to the land' means after conquest and settlement. The two sides argue back and forth about whether מלך and ביכורים are two verses that teach the same thing. The גמרא then asks why the word מושב is written by שבת, חלב ודם, and מצה ומרור, and why ביאה is written by תפילין and פטר חמור, and it gives each word a job. Finally it begins a proof from a פסוק in יהושע about eating the new grain, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: But the verse says both 'coming' and 'dwelling'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל's example verse about נסכים contains both ביאה and מושב, not only מושב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But 'coming' and 'dwelling' are both written in those verses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that רבי ישמעאל's proof verse does not fit his rule. His rule was about the word מושב, but the verse uses both ביאה and מושב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל said that wherever מושב appears, the מצוה starts only after ירושה and ישיבה. But the נסכים verse (במדבר 15:2) says 'when you come into the land of your dwellings', which has both words. So maybe the delay comes from the word ביאה, and the verse proves nothing about מושב alone.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Coming' (into the land): the Torah's wording 'when you come'
'Dwelling': the Torah's wording 'in your dwellings'
It is written about them

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a question that started just before this text. It is a challenge, not a statement.

phrases.english: Coming and dwelling are both written about them?!
phrases.notes: This is the נסכים verse: 'When you come into the land of your dwellings' (במדבר 15:2).

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּיאָה וּמוֹשָׁב כְּתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the גמרא's analysis of רבי ישמעאל's ברייתא from before this text.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's rule that the word מושב alone means 'after settlement'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof verse has both ביאה and מושב, so it cannot prove anything about מושב alone.

steps.title: The rule applies only when both words appear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: the rule is that wherever ביאה and מושב appear together, the מצוה applies only after ירושה and ישיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: wherever 'coming' and 'dwelling' are both stated, the מצוה applies only after inheritance and settlement. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing how we read רבי ישמעאל. His rule needs both words together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is narrowed. מושב by itself does not delay a מצוה. Only the pair ביאה plus מושב does. Now the נסכים verse fits the rule perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means': the גמרא rereads an earlier text
Inheritance: conquering the land
Settlement: living in the land after dividing it

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
To teach that every place
where coming and dwelling are stated
it applies only after inheritance and settlement,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by narrowing the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought מושב alone means 'after settlement'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only ביאה and מושב together mean 'after settlement'.

steps.title: Then why didn't רבי ישמעאל answer רבי עקיבא this way?
steps.stepSummary: If the rule needs both words, רבי ישמעאל could have answered רבי עקיבא's question from שבת simply by saying 'שבת only says מושב'. Why did he answer with a קל וחומר instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, רבי עקיבא said to him: 'But שבת says "dwellings"!' and he answered: 'שבת comes from a קל וחומר.' Let him instead say: 'I am only talking about where coming and dwelling both appear!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new reading from step 2 against a known exchange between רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל. If step 2 is right, רבי ישמעאל picked the wrong answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא challenged: שבת is written with מושבות, yet שבת obviously applied right away. רבי ישמעאל answered that שבת's rule comes from a קל וחומר. But according to step 2, he had an easier answer: the שבת verse has only מושב, not ביאה, so his rule never applied to it.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem with what was just said
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
Let him say to him: 'he should have answered…'
Dwellings (plural of מושב)

phrases.english: If so,
Rabbi Akiva said to him:
But there is Shabbat, where "dwellings" is stated,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: שַׁבָּת קַל וָחוֹמֶר הִיא,
phrases.english: and he said to him: Shabbat is learned from a kal vachomer,
phrases.notes: 'He' here is רבי ישמעאל answering רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: Let him say to him:
I am talking about coming and dwelling!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי ישמעאל's rule needs both ביאה and מושב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were his rule, he would have answered the שבת challenge with it, not with a קל וחומר.

steps.title: He gave one answer and then a second one
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל did use that answer, and then added a second: even if you push me on שבת's מושבות, שבת comes from a קל וחומר anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told him one point and another. One: I am only talking about where coming and dwelling both appear. And another: as for what you said about שבת having 'dwellings', שבת is learned from a קל וחומר anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל really gave two answers, and the ברייתא only quoted the second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer is the basic one: the שבת verse lacks ביאה, so the rule does not apply. The second is an extra layer: even apart from that, שבת's law is known from a קל וחומר. So the reading from step 2 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One, and another': giving two reasons for the same point

phrases.english: He was telling him one point and another:
One, that I am talking about coming and dwelling.
And another: regarding what you said,
'But there is Shabbat, where "dwellings" is stated':
Shabbat is learned from a kal vachomer.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא וְעוֹד קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל seemed to skip the easier answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said both answers; the ברייתא recorded the second.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ישמעאל, a מצוה waits for ירושה and ישיבה only when the Torah says both ביאה and מושב.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא actually disagree about in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for the concrete case where the two תנאים would rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have seen how each reads the words. Now the גמרא wants to know which real-life הלכה depends on it.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the reading is settled, it asks for the practical difference.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case of disagreement between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Were נסכים brought in the desert?
steps.stepSummary: They disagree whether נסכים were brought in the מדבר: רבי ישמעאל says no, רבי עקיבא says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about whether they offered נסכים in the מדבר. רבי ישמעאל holds they did not. רבי עקיבא holds they did.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical difference: the מצוה of נסכים during the forty years in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the נסכים verse has both ביאה and מושב, so נסכים started only after settling the land. רבי עקיבא does not read the verse that way, so for him נסכים were already brought in the מדבר.

keyTerms.meaning: Libations: wine (with flour and oil) brought along with קרבנות
The desert, where the Jews spent forty years
They offered (brought as a קרבן)
Holds, is of the opinion

phrases.english: They disagree about whether they offered libations in the desert.
Rabbi Yishmael holds:
They did not offer libations in the desert.
And Rabbi Akiva holds:
They did offer libations in the desert.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּקֵירְבוּ נְסָכִים בַּמִּדְבָּר קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical difference is whether נסכים were brought in the מדבר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל: no נסכים in the מדבר. רבי עקיבא: there were נסכים in the מדבר.

steps.title: אביי: two teachings from רבי ישמעאל's school clash
steps.stepSummary: אביי says this teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל disagrees with another teaching from the same school.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: this תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל differs from another תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new point and sets up the next move: he will show another teaching from רבי ישמעאל's school that does not match this one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, the school of רבי ישמעאל says a מצוה is delayed only when ביאה and מושב appear together. אביי is telling us that a different תנא from the same school holds otherwise. The next step quotes that other teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher from the study hall (school) of רבי ישמעאל
Goes out from the other: differs from another opinion

phrases.english: Abaye said:
This tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael

phrases.aramaic: מַפֵּיק מֵאִידַּךְ תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.english: differs from the other tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael.
phrases.notes: 'This tanna' is the one we just learned, who needs both 'coming' and 'dwelling'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַאי תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל מַפֵּיק מֵאִידַּךְ תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line comparing the step 2 reading with another teaching from the same school.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The teaching that both ביאה and מושב are needed differs from another teaching of רבי ישמעאל's school.

steps.title: The second teaching: every 'coming to the land' means after conquest and settlement
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that since the תורה spelled out 'after inheritance and settling' for one מצוה (מלך), every unspecified 'coming to the land' means the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: The תורה often says 'when you come to the land' without explaining when that is. In one place it spelled it out: after you inherit the land and settle it. So the same is true everywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל that אביי was talking about. This is the teaching that clashes with the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching learns one general rule from one example, the מצוה of a מלך, where the פסוק says 'and you inherit it and settle it.' If so, every 'coming to the land' is delayed until after conquest and settlement. You would not need the extra word מושבות to teach this, and that is why it clashes with the first teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Comings': the places where the תורה says 'when you come to the land'
Without detail; stated generally
Spelled out, specified
Inheriting (conquering) the land and settling in it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic case of learning a general rule from one specific case. The next steps test whether that kind of learning is allowed here.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Since 'comings' are stated in the Torah without detail,
and the verse spelled out for you in one of them
phrases.notes: This is the מצוה of appointing a king: דברים 17:14.

phrases.english: that it means after inheritance and settling,
so too, all of them mean after inheritance and settling.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the second teaching that אביי said disagrees with the first one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every unspecified 'coming to the land' means after conquest and settlement, learned from מלך.

steps.title: The other side: מלך and ביכורים are two verses that say the same thing, so they cannot teach
steps.stepSummary: The תנא of the first teaching does not learn from מלך, because ביכורים also says 'after inheritance and settling.' Two verses that teach the same thing cannot be used to teach other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other תנא does not learn this way. That is because both מלך and ביכורים say this. When two verses come to teach the same thing, we cannot learn other cases from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תנא of the first teaching (in the argument with רבי עקיבא) does not accept the learning from מלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that when the תורה repeats the same detail in two places, the repetition shows the detail belongs only to those two cases. So the detail of 'inheritance and settling' would stay with מלך and ביכורים, and would not spread to every 'coming to the land.' That is why this תנא needed a separate source, the word מושבות.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: the other תנא or opinion
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
Two verses that come to teach the same thing
They do not teach other cases

steps.confusionAlert: Saying 'two verses do not teach' does not mean the rule is untrue for מלך and ביכורים. It still applies to them. It just cannot be spread to other מצוות.

phrases.english: And the other tanna:
phrases.notes: This is the תנא of the first teaching, the one in the argument with רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: because king and first fruits are
phrases.notes: ביכורים also says 'and you inherit it and settle in it': דברים 26:1.

phrases.english: two verses that come as one,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד אֵין מְלַמְּדִין.
phrases.english: and any two verses that come as one do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה מֶלֶךְ וּבִיכּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the first teaching rejects the learning from מלך given in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning a general rule from מלך.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מלך and ביכורים repeat the same detail, so they are שני כתובים הבאים כאחד and cannot teach other cases.

steps.title: Both verses are needed, so they can still teach
steps.stepSummary: The second teaching answers that מלך and ביכורים are each needed. Without one, we would have thought that case comes right away, so they are not a pointless repeat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other answers: both are needed. If the תורה wrote only מלך, I would say ביכורים must be brought right away, since the person is enjoying the fruit. If it wrote only ביכורים, I would say a king must be appointed right away, since a king's job is to conquer.
steps.whatsHappening: The second teaching defends itself. It argues that the two verses are not a repeat, because each one teaches something we could not learn from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of שני כתובים only applies if one verse could have been learned from the other. Here each case has its own reason to come right away: ביכורים because the person is already benefiting from the fruit, and מלך because a king is needed to lead the conquest. Since each verse is needed, the rule can still be learned from them for all other cases.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed: each verse teaches something of its own
I would have thought
He benefits, enjoys
Immediately
To conquer

phrases.english: And the other: they are both needed,
phrases.notes: Now the other side speaks: the second teaching, the one אביי brought.

phrases.english: for if the Merciful One had written king
and not written first fruits,
I would have said:
first fruits, since he benefits, must be brought immediately.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי כְּתַב בִּיכּוּרִים וְלָא כְּתַב מֶלֶךְ,
phrases.english: And if it had written first fruits and not king,
I would have said:
a king, whose way is to conquer, is appointed immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: צְרִיכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's claim that מלך and ביכורים are a repeat that cannot teach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each verse is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only one verse, the other case would come immediately: ביכורים because of the benefit, מלך because of the conquest.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both verses are needed, so they are not שני כתובים הבאים כאחד and can teach every other 'coming to the land.'

steps.title: No, ביכורים could be learned from מלך with a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The first side pushes back: the תורה could have written only מלך, and ביכורים would follow by קל וחומר. So ביכורים is not really needed, and the two verses still cannot teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other answers: the תורה could have written only מלך, and ביכורים would not be needed. I would reason: if a king, whose job is to conquer, waits until after inheritance and settling, then ביכורים should surely wait too.
steps.whatsHappening: The first side attacks the 'both are needed' answer. It shows that one of the two verses could have been learned by logic alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a king, who is needed for the conquest itself, waits until after conquest and settlement, then ביכורים, which has nothing to do with conquering, should surely wait. So the ביכורים verse adds nothing, and the two verses are again a repeat that cannot teach other cases. This keeps the first teaching's position that a separate source like מושבות is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Merciful One write: the תורה could have written
And if: the opening of a קל וחומר
All the more so

steps.whatToRemember: The argument turns on whether ביכורים could be learned from מלך. The second teaching says each verse is needed, so every 'coming to the land' is after conquest and settlement. The first teaching says ביכורים follows from מלך by קל וחומר, so the two verses repeat each other and cannot teach.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'ואידך' switches back again. It is the first teaching (from the argument with רבי עקיבא) speaking, not the one from step 10.

phrases.english: And the other:
Let the Merciful One write king
and first fruits would not be needed,
and I would say:
And if a king, who is there to conquer,
is appointed only after inheritance and settling,
first fruits, all the more so, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: נִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא מֶלֶךְ וְלָא בָּעֵי בִּיכּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10 by showing the ביכורים verse was not needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 10 that both מלך and ביכורים are needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ביכורים follows from מלך by קל וחומר, so it was not needed, and the two verses remain שני כתובים הבאים כאחד.

steps.title: The ביכורים verse is needed so we don't compare it to חלה
steps.stepSummary: The second teaching answers the challenge from step 11. If only מלך were written, we would have said ביכורים is like חלה and starts immediately, so the ביכורים verse is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side answers: if the תורה had written 'after inheritance and settling' only by מלך, I would have said ביכורים is like חלה, which applied right away. So the תורה had to write it by ביכורים too.
steps.whatsHappening: The side that learns from מלך defends itself. It shows that the ביכורים verse is not extra after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said ביכורים could be learned from מלך by a קל וחומר, so its own verse is wasted. The answer is that a different comparison would have won: ביכורים is a gift from produce, just like חלה, and חלה started right when they entered the land. So the ביכורים verse is needed to tell us to wait, and the two verses are not a pointless repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other side of the argument)
It is just like; a comparison to another case
The piece of dough given to a כהן, which applied as soon as they entered the land
It teaches us (that the conclusion we would have reached is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the תנא אביי quoted, each verse about 'after inheritance and settling' is really needed: without the ביכורים verse, we would have compared ביכורים to חלה. So מלך and ביכורים can teach every other 'coming to the land.' The other תנא disagrees and needs both ביאה and מושב.

phrases.english: And the other one:
phrases.notes: This is the teaching that learns from מלך, answering the challenge from step 11.

phrases.english: If [the תורה] had written it this way [only by מלך],
I would have said:
it is just like חלה,
phrases.notes: חלה applied as soon as they entered the land, so ביכורים would have started right away too.

phrases.english: so it teaches us [otherwise].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: אִי כְּתַב הָכִי הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11, which said ביכורים could be learned from מלך by קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the verse is needed because a different comparison (חלה) would otherwise win
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without its own verse, ביכורים would be like חלה and apply immediately upon entering the land.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ביכורים verse is needed, so מלך and ביכורים are not two verses teaching the same thing, and they can teach about other מצוות.

steps.title: Why does the תורה write 'מושב' by שבת?
steps.stepSummary: If a חובת הגוף applies everywhere anyway, the word 'מושב' by שבת seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said a מצוה on the body applies both in ארץ ישראל and outside it, why does the תורה need to write 'in all your dwellings' by שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It asks why the word 'מושב' is written by שבת if it already applies everywhere. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a חובת הגוף (a מצוה that is on the person, not on the land) applies everywhere. שבת is clearly a חובת הגוף, so the word 'מושב' would seem to add nothing. The גמרא wants to know what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: And now that you have said
A מצוה that is an obligation on the person, not tied to the land
Outside ארץ ישראל
Dwelling; the word 'בכל מושבותיכם', in all your dwellings
Why do I need it? (asking what a word adds)

phrases.english: And now that you have said
that an obligation of the body applies

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: both in ארץ ישראל and outside the land,
the word 'dwelling' that the Merciful One wrote by שבת,
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ חוֹבַת הַגּוּף נוֹהֶגֶת בֵּין בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ביכורים discussion and goes back to the general rule that a חובת הגוף applies everywhere, asking about the word 'מושב'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word 'מושב' by שבת teach, if שבת already applies everywhere as a חובת הגוף?

steps.title: 'מושב' teaches that שבת does not depend on בית דין
steps.stepSummary: Since שבת appears in the section of the Festivals, we might have thought it needs בית דין to set it, like the Festivals. 'מושב' teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since שבת is written in the section about the Festivals, it should need sanctifying like the Festivals. So the תורה teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'מושב' by שבת was needed to block a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dates of the Festivals depend on בית דין declaring the new month. Because שבת is listed together with the Festivals, we might have tied it to בית דין too. 'מושב' tells us שבת comes on its own every seventh day, wherever a Jew lives.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
It would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken thought)
In the section about the Festivals
Sanctifying, here meaning בית דין setting the date

phrases.english: It was needed,
since it would enter your mind to say:
since it is written in the section of the Festivals,
it should need sanctifying like the Festivals,
phrases.notes: The Festivals' dates depend on בית דין declaring the new month.

phrases.english: so it teaches us [that it does not].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּבְעִנְיָנָא דְמוֹעֲדוֹת כְּתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מושב' by שבת teaches that שבת does not need sanctifying by בית דין like the Festivals.

steps.title: Why does the תורה write 'מושב' by חלב and blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the prohibition of חלב ודם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the word 'dwelling' that the תורה wrote about forbidden fat and blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question again, now about חלב ודם. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not eating חלב ודם is also a חובת הגוף, so it should apply everywhere anyway. So what does 'מושב' add here?

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat of an animal
Blood, which is forbidden to eat
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: The word 'dwelling' that the Merciful One wrote
by forbidden fat and blood, why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״מוֹשָׁב״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּי חֵלֶב וָדָם, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question as step 13, now applied to חלב ודם.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'מושב' by חלב ודם teach, if it already applies everywhere?

steps.title: 'מושב' teaches that חלב and blood stay forbidden without קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: Since חלב ודם are written in the section of קרבנות, we might have thought they are forbidden only when there are קרבנות. 'מושב' teaches that they are always forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since they are written in the section of offerings, when there are offerings, fat and blood are forbidden, and when there are no offerings, they are not. So the תורה teaches us that they are always forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'מושב' by חלב ודם blocks the idea that the prohibition depends on the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fat and blood are what go on the מזבח, so we might have linked the prohibition to the times when קרבנות are brought. 'מושב' cuts that link. The prohibition stays even when there is no בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: In the section about offerings
At a time when there is
At a time when there is not
Should be forbidden

phrases.english: It was needed, since it would enter your mind to say:
since they are written in the section of offerings,
when there are offerings,
fat and blood should be forbidden,
but when there are no offerings, they are not,
so it teaches us [that they are always forbidden].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּבְעִנְיָנָא דְקׇרְבָּנוֹת כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מושב' teaches that חלב ודם are forbidden even when there are no קרבנות.

steps.title: Why does the תורה write 'מושב' by מצה and מרור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question a third time, about מצה ומרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need the word 'dwelling' that the תורה wrote about מצה and מרור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks its third 'why do I need it' question, now about מצה ומרור. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating מצה ומרור is a חובת הגוף, which already applies everywhere. So again, what does 'מושב' add?

keyTerms.meaning: Unleavened bread eaten on פסח
Bitter herbs eaten on פסח

phrases.english: The word 'dwelling' that the Merciful One wrote
by מצה and מרור, why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״מוֹשָׁב״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּי מַצָּה וּמָרוֹר, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question as steps 13 and 15, now applied to מצה ומרור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'מושב' by מצה ומרור teach, if it already applies everywhere?

steps.title: 'מושב' teaches that מצה and מרור apply even without the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: Since the פסוק says to eat the פסח with מצה ומרור, we might have thought they apply only when there is a קרבן פסח. 'מושב' teaches that they apply every year.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since it is written 'with מצות and bitter herbs they shall eat it,' when there is a קרבן פסח, yes, and when there is no קרבן פסח, no. So the תורה teaches us that the מצוה applies even then.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'מושב' by מצה ומרור blocks the idea that they depend on the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק makes מצה ומרור sound like side dishes for the קרבן פסח, so we might think: no קרבן, no מצה ומרור. 'מושב' shows the מצוה is not tied to the קרבן. It applies wherever and whenever Jews live, even without a בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is written
They shall eat it (the קרבן פסח)
Here, the קרבן פסח
Yes

steps.whatToRemember: All three 'מושב' words have the same pattern. Each one blocks a mistaken link: שבת to בית דין, חלב ודם to קרבנות, and מצה ומרור to the קרבן פסח. These מצוות apply everywhere, at all times.

phrases.english: It was needed, since it would enter your mind to say
that since it is written:
'With מצות and bitter herbs they shall eat it,'
when there is a קרבן פסח, yes,
when there is no קרבן פסח, no,
so it teaches us [that they apply even then].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב ״עַל מַצּוֹת וּמְרֹרִים יֹאכְלֻהוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 and finishes the series of 'מושב' questions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'מושב' teaches that the מצוה of מצה ומרור applies even when there is no קרבן פסח.

steps.title: Why is 'coming into the land' written for תפילין and פטר חמור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תורה writes the word ביאה ('when ה׳ brings you into the land') in the section about תפילין and פטר חמור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'coming' that the תורה wrote about תפילין and the firstborn donkey: why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks one more 'why is this word needed' question. This time it is about the word ביאה, which appears in the section of תפילין and פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually ביאה ('when you come into the land') suggests that a מצוה only starts after entering ארץ ישראל. But the question assumes that תפילין and פטר חמור are not limited that way. So the word seems to have no job, and the גמרא wants to know what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Coming' into the land, from the phrase 'when ה׳ brings you'
'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה or ה׳
תפילין: the boxes with פסוקים worn on the head and arm
The firstborn of a donkey, which must be redeemed
'Why do I need it?' A question about why a word is there

phrases.english: The word "coming" that the Merciful One wrote
phrases.notes: שמות 13:11, 'וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִאֲךָ', which opens the section on these מצוות.

phrases.english: regarding tefillin and the firstborn donkey
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בִּיאָה״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּי תְּפִילִּין וּפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of 'why is this word needed' questions. The earlier questions were about מושב, and this one is about ביאה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word ביאה teach in the section on תפילין and פטר חמור?

steps.title: The word teaches that this מצוה earns entry into the land
steps.stepSummary: The word ביאה is needed for the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל: do this מצוה, and because of it you will enter the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed for what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Do this מצוה, because in its merit you will enter the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that here ביאה does not limit the מצוה to ארץ ישראל. Instead, it teaches about reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read as a promise, not as a starting time. Keeping this מצוה is the reason you will be brought into the land. So the word has a job, and the מצוה is not tied only to living in ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is needed for', meaning the word is used to teach something else
A teaching from the study house of רבי ישמעאל
Because of it, in its merit

steps.whatToRemember: Not every 'when you come into the land' limits a מצוה to ארץ ישראל. By תפילין and פטר חמור, it teaches that the מצוה is what earns entry into the land.

phrases.english: That word is needed
for what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught
Do this מצוה
for because of it you will enter the land

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19 by giving the word ביאה a different job.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ביאה here teaches a reward: doing the מצוה brings one into the land.

steps.title: A פסוק in יהושע fits the view that 'מושב' means wherever you dwell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a proof. According to the view that 'מושב' means wherever you live, it makes sense that the Jews ate the produce of the land only on the day after פסח and not before. The argument continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who says 'מושב' means wherever you dwell, that is why it is written: 'And they ate of the produce of the land on the day after פסח.' On the day after פסח they ate, but before that they did not eat. Apparently...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about what the word מושב means. It uses a פסוק in יהושע. This is a setup line: it shows which view fits the פסוק, so it can raise a challenge against the other view next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מושב means 'wherever you dwell,' the new grain was forbidden as soon as the Jews entered the land. That explains why they waited until the day after פסח to eat it. The word אלמא ('apparently') shows that the גמרא is about to draw a conclusion from this, which will make trouble for the other view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted' or 'it works well for'. It sets up a contrast with a view that does not work as well
'Dwelling', from the phrase 'in all your dwelling places'
The produce of the land
On the day after פסח
'Apparently' or 'this shows that'. It introduces a conclusion

steps.confusionAlert: בשלמא does not mean the גמרא has decided in favor of this view. It means 'this view works fine,' and it hints that the other view will be challenged.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says that "dwelling"
means wherever you dwell
that is why it is written
"And they ate of the produce of the land on the day after the Pesach"
on the day after Pesach they ate
before that, they did not eat
Apparently...

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר ״מוֹשָׁב״ כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתֶּם יוֹשְׁבִים מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining why words are needed to a new discussion about the meaning of מושב, using a פסוק from יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that does not read מושב as 'wherever you dwell'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows that the new grain was forbidden right after entering the land, until the day after פסח. This fits 'wherever you dwell,' and it sets up a difficulty for the other view.
